ja: 現存する世界最古級の会社は大阪の金剛組で、578年創業とされる。寺社建築の会社で、四天王寺の建立に関わったと伝えられる。
easy: One of the oldest companies in the world is Kongo Gumi in Osaka. It started in the year 578 and builds temples.
std: Kongo Gumi, an Osaka temple builder said to have been founded in 578, is often cited as one of the oldest continuously operating companies in the world.

ja: 世界で初めて株式を一般に発行した会社の一つは、1602年に設立されたオランダ東インド会社。アムステルダムで株が売買された。
easy: The Dutch East India Company, started in 1602, was one of the first companies to sell shares to the public.
std: The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, was among the first companies to issue shares to the public, which were traded in Amsterdam.

ja: 大阪・堂島の米市場では、江戸時代に「将来の米」を売買する取引が行われていた。世界で最初期の先物市場の一つとされる。
easy: In the 1700s, traders in Osaka bought and sold rice for the future. It was one of the first futures markets in the world.
std: The Dojima Rice Exchange in Osaka, which traded contracts on future rice in the 18th century, is often described as one of the world's first organized futures markets.

ja: 株価が上がる相場を「ブル（雄牛）」、下がる相場を「ベア（熊）」と呼ぶ。雄牛は角を突き上げ、熊は前足を振り下ろして攻撃することに由来するという説がある。
easy: A rising market is called a 'bull' market, and a falling one is a 'bear' market.
std: Rising markets are called 'bull' markets and falling ones 'bear' markets; one popular explanation is that a bull thrusts its horns up while a bear swipes its paws down.

ja: 世界初の汎用クレジットカードとされるダイナースクラブカードは、1950年にアメリカで生まれた。財布を忘れて食事代を払えなかった体験がきっかけと伝えられる。
easy: The Diners Club card, started in 1950, is called the first general credit card. The idea came after a man forgot his wallet at dinner.
std: The Diners Club card, launched in 1950, is often called the first general-purpose charge card; its founder reportedly got the idea after forgetting his wallet at a restaurant.

ja: Google の名前は、10の100乗を表す数学用語「googol」のつづりを変えたもの。膨大な情報を整理するという目標を表している。
easy: The name Google comes from 'googol', a very large number: 1 followed by 100 zeros.
std: Google's name is a play on 'googol', the number 1 followed by 100 zeros, reflecting its aim to organize a huge amount of information.

ja: ニンテンドーは1889年に京都で花札を作る会社として始まった。ゲーム機を作るようになったのは、それから80年以上後のこと。
easy: Nintendo started in 1889 in Kyoto as a company that made playing cards.
std: Nintendo was founded in Kyoto in 1889 as a maker of hanafuda playing cards, decades before it entered the video game business.

ja: Amazon は1994年に創業し、最初はインターネットで本だけを売る会社だった。
easy: Amazon started in 1994. At first, it only sold books on the internet.
std: Amazon was founded in 1994 and began as an online bookstore before expanding into almost every kind of product.

ja: 1929年10月のニューヨーク株式市場の大暴落は、世界恐慌の始まりとされる。アメリカの失業率は1933年に約25％に達した。
easy: The stock market crash of 1929 helped start the Great Depression. By 1933, about one in four American workers had no job.
std: The Wall Street Crash of October 1929 marked the beginning of the Great Depression; US unemployment reached about 25 percent by 1933.

ja: 1630年代のオランダでは、チューリップの球根の値段が異常に高くなった。「チューリップ・バブル」は歴史上の投機熱の例としてよく語られる。
easy: In the 1630s in the Netherlands, tulip bulbs became very expensive. This is often called the first big price bubble.
std: In the 1630s, prices for tulip bulbs in the Dutch Republic soared and then collapsed; 'tulip mania' is often cited as an early example of a speculative bubble.

ja: 日本初のコンビニの一つとされるセブン-イレブンの1号店は、1974年に東京・豊洲に開店した。
easy: The first 7-Eleven store in Japan opened in Toyosu, Tokyo, in 1974.
std: Japan's first 7-Eleven store opened in Toyosu, Tokyo, in 1974, helping to launch the country's convenience store culture.

ja: 「パレートの法則（80対20の法則）」は、結果の約8割が原因の約2割から生まれるという経験則。イタリアの経済学者パレートの観察にちなむ。
easy: The 80/20 rule says that about 80% of results often come from about 20% of causes.
std: The Pareto principle, or 80/20 rule, observes that roughly 80 percent of effects often come from 20 percent of causes; it is named after the economist Vilfredo Pareto.

ja: トヨタの「かんばん方式」は、必要なものを必要なときに必要なだけ作る仕組み。スーパーマーケットの品出しの仕方から着想を得たと言われる。
easy: Toyota's 'kanban' system makes only what is needed, when it is needed. The idea came partly from how supermarkets fill shelves.
std: Toyota's kanban system, part of just-in-time production, was reportedly inspired by the way American supermarkets restocked shelves only as items were sold.

ja: 複式簿記を初めて本で詳しく紹介したのは、1494年のイタリアの数学者ルカ・パチョーリ。今も会計の基本になっている。
easy: In 1494, an Italian named Luca Pacioli wrote about double-entry bookkeeping. Accountants still use this method today.
std: Luca Pacioli's 1494 book was the first printed work to describe double-entry bookkeeping in detail, the system still at the heart of accounting.

ja: 世界最古の硬貨の一つは、紀元前600年ごろに今のトルコにあったリディア王国で作られた。金と銀の混ざった「エレクトラム」でできていた。
easy: Some of the first coins were made around 600 BC in Lydia, in what is now Turkey.
std: Some of the earliest known coins were minted around 600 BC in the kingdom of Lydia, in modern Turkey, from electrum, a natural mix of gold and silver.

ja: 世界最古の紙幣は、11世紀の中国（宋）で使われた「交子」とされる。
easy: The first paper money was used in China about 1,000 years ago.
std: The first government-issued paper money, the jiaozi, appeared in Song dynasty China in the 11th century.

ja: 現存する世界最古の銀行は、1472年創業のイタリアのモンテ・デイ・パスキ・ディ・シエナとされる。
easy: The oldest bank still working today is in Siena, Italy. It started in 1472.
std: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena, founded in 1472, is generally considered the oldest bank still in operation.

ja: GDP（国内総生産）は、一定期間に国内で生み出された財とサービスの付加価値の合計。今のような考え方は1930年代にアメリカで整えられた。
easy: GDP is the total value of goods and services a country makes in a year. The idea was developed in the 1930s.
std: Gross domestic product measures the total value added by goods and services produced in a country over a period; the modern concept was developed in the 1930s.

ja: ジンバブエでは2000年代後半に物価が極端に上がり、2008年には100兆ジンバブエ・ドル紙幣が発行された。
easy: In 2008, prices in Zimbabwe rose so fast that the country printed a 100 trillion dollar bill.
std: During Zimbabwe's hyperinflation in the late 2000s, the central bank issued a 100-trillion-dollar banknote in 2008.

ja: そろばんは日本では室町時代ごろに中国から伝わったとされ、江戸時代には寺子屋で「読み・書き・そろばん」として広く教えられた。
easy: The abacus came to Japan from China long ago. In the Edo period, children learned reading, writing, and the abacus.
std: The abacus is thought to have reached Japan from China around the 15th or 16th century, and in the Edo period it was widely taught alongside reading and writing.

ja: ショッピングカートは1937年にアメリカのスーパーの経営者シルヴァン・ゴールドマンが考えた。客が多くの品物を買えるようにするためだった。
easy: The shopping cart was invented in 1937 by a supermarket owner in the US. He wanted customers to buy more.
std: The shopping cart was invented in 1937 by Sylvan Goldman, an Oklahoma supermarket owner who wanted customers to be able to carry more goods.

ja: バーコード（UPC）で初めて読み取られた商品は、1974年にアメリカのスーパーで売られたチューインガムだった。
easy: The first product scanned with a barcode was a pack of chewing gum in 1974.
std: The first product sold using a UPC barcode scan was a pack of Wrigley's chewing gum, in an Ohio supermarket in 1974.

ja: セブン-イレブンの名前は、もともと朝7時から夜11時まで営業していたことから。
easy: 7-Eleven got its name because stores were open from 7 am to 11 pm.
std: 7-Eleven took its name from its original opening hours, 7 a.m. to 11 p.m.

ja: 「スパム」（迷惑メール）の名前は、缶詰肉スパムを連呼するイギリスのコメディ番組の場面から来ている。
easy: Junk email is called 'spam' because of a funny TV sketch where people keep saying 'Spam'.
std: Unwanted email is called 'spam' after a Monty Python sketch in which the name of the canned meat is repeated over and over.

ja: ロンドンの保険市場ロイズは、17世紀にエドワード・ロイドが開いたコーヒーハウスで、船主や商人が集まったことから始まった。
easy: Lloyd's of London, a famous insurance market, began in a coffee house in the 1680s.
std: Lloyd's of London grew out of Edward Lloyd's coffee house in the late 17th century, where ship owners and merchants met to arrange insurance.

ja: ニューヨーク証券取引所の始まりは、1792年に24人の株式仲買人がウォール街のスズカケノキの下で結んだ「ボタンウッド協定」とされる。
easy: The New York Stock Exchange began in 1792 when 24 traders made an agreement under a tree on Wall Street.
std: The New York Stock Exchange traces its origins to the 1792 Buttonwood Agreement, signed by 24 brokers under a buttonwood tree on Wall Street.

ja: ウォール街の名前は、17世紀にオランダ人がそこに築いた木の壁（wall）に由来する。
easy: Wall Street got its name from a wooden wall that was built there in the 1600s.
std: Wall Street is named after a wooden wall that Dutch settlers built along its route in the 17th century.

ja: 世界で初めてフランチャイズ方式を大規模に広げた例の一つは、19世紀のシンガーミシンの販売網とされる。
easy: One of the first big franchise systems was used to sell Singer sewing machines in the 1800s.
std: The Singer sewing machine company is often credited with one of the first large-scale franchise systems in the 19th century.

ja: アメリカで週40時間労働を早くから取り入れた企業の一つがフォード。1926年に週5日・40時間制を導入した。
easy: In 1926, Ford was one of the first companies to give workers a five-day, 40-hour week.
std: In 1926, the Ford Motor Company became one of the first major employers to adopt a five-day, 40-hour work week.

ja: フォードは1913年に移動式の組み立てラインを導入し、T型フォード1台を作る時間を約12時間から約1時間半に縮めた。
easy: In 1913, Ford started using a moving assembly line. A car could be made in about 90 minutes instead of 12 hours.
std: Ford's moving assembly line, introduced in 1913, cut the time to build a Model T from about 12 hours to roughly an hour and a half.

ja: 目標の立て方「SMART」は、具体的・測定できる・達成できる・関連がある・期限がある、の頭文字。1981年の論文で紹介された。
easy: SMART goals are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound.
std: The SMART framework for goals—Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound—was introduced in a 1981 management article.

ja: PDCA（計画・実行・評価・改善）は、品質管理で知られるデミングが日本で広めた考え方がもとになっている。
easy: PDCA means Plan, Do, Check, Act. It is a cycle for making work better step by step.
std: The PDCA cycle—Plan, Do, Check, Act—is associated with W. Edwards Deming, whose quality-control ideas were highly influential in postwar Japan.

ja: 「カイゼン（改善）」は英語にもなった日本語。現場で少しずつ改良を重ねる考え方として、世界の工場で使われている。
easy: 'Kaizen' is a Japanese word used in English. It means making small improvements all the time.
std: 'Kaizen', the Japanese term for continuous improvement through small changes, has been adopted in English and in factories worldwide.

ja: 3M のポスト・イットは、強力な接着剤を作ろうとして失敗した「弱い接着剤」から生まれた。
easy: Post-it Notes came from a failed try at making a very strong glue.
std: Post-it Notes grew out of a 3M scientist's failed attempt to make a super-strong adhesive, which instead produced a weak, reusable one.

ja: マクドナルドは、1940年にアメリカでマクドナルド兄弟が開いた1軒の店から始まった。
easy: McDonald's started in 1940 as one restaurant run by two brothers in the US.
std: McDonald's began in 1940 as a single restaurant opened by brothers Richard and Maurice McDonald in California.

ja: ナイキの社名は、ギリシャ神話の勝利の女神ニケ（Nike）から取られた。
easy: Nike is named after the Greek goddess of victory.
std: Nike takes its name from Nike, the winged goddess of victory in Greek mythology.

ja: 「ピザ2枚ルール」はアマゾンで知られる考え方で、チームはピザ2枚で足りる人数に抑えるのがよいとする。
easy: Amazon's 'two-pizza rule' says a team should be small enough to share two pizzas.
std: Amazon's 'two-pizza team' rule holds that a team should be small enough to be fed by two pizzas, keeping communication simple.

ja: 「ブレインストーミング」は、アメリカの広告会社の経営者アレックス・オズボーンが1940〜50年代に広めた会議の方法。
easy: Brainstorming was made popular by an advertising executive, Alex Osborn, in the 1940s and 1950s.
std: Brainstorming as a group technique was popularized by advertising executive Alex Osborn in the 1940s and 1950s.

ja: 「CEO（最高経営責任者）」という肩書きがアメリカで広く使われるようになったのは、主に1970年代以降。
easy: The title 'CEO' became common in American companies mainly after the 1970s.
std: The title 'chief executive officer' became widespread in American corporations largely from the 1970s onward.

ja: 握手の習慣は古代から見られ、武器を持っていないことを示すためという説がよく知られている。
easy: People have shaken hands for thousands of years. One idea is that it showed you had no weapon.
std: Handshakes date back to ancient times; a popular theory says they began as a way to show that one's hand held no weapon.

ja: ペーパークリップの今の形「ジェム型」は、19世紀末のイギリスのジェム社が売り出したとされ、特許を取った人ははっきりしていない。
easy: The common paper clip shape is called the 'Gem' clip. It came from Britain in the late 1800s.
std: The familiar double-loop paper clip, known as the Gem clip, appeared in Britain in the late 19th century, and its original inventor is uncertain.

ja: ファクスの原理は1843年にスコットランドの時計職人アレクサンダー・ベインが特許を取っており、電話（1876年）より古い。
easy: The idea of the fax machine is older than the telephone. It was patented in 1843.
std: The basic principle of the fax machine was patented by Scottish inventor Alexander Bain in 1843, decades before the telephone.

ja: 日経平均株価は1989年12月29日に3万8915円の最高値をつけた後、大きく下がり、この値を超えたのは2024年2月だった。
easy: The Nikkei stock average hit a record at the end of 1989. It took until 2024 to go higher.
std: Japan's Nikkei 225 peaked at 38,915 on December 29, 1989, and did not surpass that level again until February 2024.

ja: 世界貿易機関（WTO）は1995年に発足した。前身は1947年に結ばれた関税と貿易に関する一般協定（GATT）。
easy: The World Trade Organization began in 1995. Before that, there was an agreement called GATT from 1947.
std: The World Trade Organization was established in 1995, succeeding the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, signed in 1947.

ja: ユーロの紙幣と硬貨は2002年1月1日に使われ始めた。帳簿上の通貨としては1999年から存在していた。
easy: Euro notes and coins were first used on January 1, 2002.
std: Euro banknotes and coins entered circulation on January 1, 2002, although the euro had existed as an accounting currency since 1999.

ja: 世界初の現金自動預け払い機（ATM）の一つは、1967年にロンドンの銀行に設置された。
easy: One of the first cash machines (ATMs) opened in London in 1967.
std: One of the world's first cash machines was installed at a Barclays branch in London in 1967.

ja: 「タイム・イズ・マネー（時は金なり）」は、ベンジャミン・フランクリンが1748年の文章で書いた言葉として知られる。
easy: The saying 'Time is money' is known from Benjamin Franklin's writing in 1748.
std: The phrase 'Time is money' is famously associated with Benjamin Franklin, who used it in his 1748 essay 'Advice to a Young Tradesman'.

ja: 日本のお中元・お歳暮は、取引先との関係を保つ贈り物として今も多くの企業が続けている。
easy: In Japan, many companies send gifts to their business partners in summer and at the end of the year.
std: In Japan, ochugen and oseibo—gifts sent in summer and at year-end—are still exchanged by many companies to maintain business relationships.

ja: 「ブロックチェーン」の考え方を広く知らしめたのは、2008年に「サトシ・ナカモト」という名前で発表されたビットコインの論文。正体は今もわかっていない。
easy: Bitcoin was described in 2008 by someone called 'Satoshi Nakamoto'. Nobody knows for sure who that is.
std: Bitcoin was introduced in a 2008 paper by the pseudonymous 'Satoshi Nakamoto', whose real identity remains unknown.

ja: 自動販売機の歴史は古く、紀元1世紀のアレクサンドリアのヘロンが、硬貨を入れると聖水が出る装置を記録している。
easy: About 2,000 years ago, a man named Heron described a machine that gave holy water when you put in a coin.
std: The earliest known vending machine was described by Hero of Alexandria in the first century: a coin dropped in released a measure of holy water.
